.claude\rules\port-note-discipline.md:20:A port commit that adds a port-note header of N lines silently shifts every line below it by +N. Cites pointing INTO the ported file from sibling files OR self-cites within the port-note itself use UPSTREAM coordinates by reflex; no compile error fires; readers click and land in the wrong place. n=4 evidence across iter-10/12/13 of this fire's port arc demonstrates the drift class is structural, not coincidental.
.claude\rules\port-note-discipline.md:35:When adding a port-note header of N lines to a ported file, cites pointing INTO that file from anywhere (sibling files, the port-note's own self-cites, README/CLAUDE.md/rules, commit bodies) carry UPSTREAM coordinates by default. Compensate.
.claude\rules\port-note-discipline.md:44:2. **Line-bump compensation (fallback)**: when the port edit is a **pure header insertion before the cited span** (no other line additions/deletions), bump every cite by +N where N = port-note line count. Run before commit:
.claude\rules\port-note-discipline.md:46:   N=<port-note line count>
.claude\rules\port-note-discipline.md:50:   ⚠️ **Caveat**: line-bump is INVALID when the port edit involved any other content addition/deletion below the port-note. In that case, fall back to symbol-anchor or resolve-by-content (`grep <symbol> <ported_file>` to find new line, then update cite).
